title: Emergent — Research Observatory
question: How does intelligence change when part of its memory, action, or organization exists outside the agent itself?
status: curated snapshot; literature bridge and synthesis note added
notes: This public Observatory is a curated view, not a mirror of the research repository.
The map contains 17 selected model-run records. The 017 methodological note, 018 unrun protocol, and 019 interpretive synthesis are separate records and do not count as completed experiments.
The literature bridge features three directly relevant papers from a 22-paper seed index; it is not a systematic review or a claim of exhaustive coverage.
Edges state a documented relation or a clearly labelled interpretive research-direction link; thematic similarity alone is not a relation.
A click opens the source file in the research repository. Access may require repository permissions.
Simulation outputs are evidence about the specified models, not direct evidence about humans or real-world AI systems.
Statuses preserve unresolved audits, design limitations, and provisional interpretations rather than collapsing them into a single success label.

experiments.title: What a shared external memory store does to accuracy, dependence, and entrenched error
experiments.summary: A minimal simulation compares overwrite and history-based majority policies, with and without verification. Corrected metrics show the apparent cleaning effect weakens as individual competence falls.
experiments.tension: Can a shared store clean errors without making its own distortions persistent?

experiments.title: History-based cleaning collapses under correlated error
experiments.summary: The model tests independent errors, shared population bias, and mixed opposing biases. Majority history averages independent noise but cannot remove a bias shared by the population.
experiments.tension: Does diversity matter more than average individual competence?

experiments.title: Provenance filters error concentration, not error direction
experiments.summary: Writer identity is added to the shared history. Provenance-aware reading can resist a single high-frequency writer, but does not solve shared bias. One cross-condition comparison has a documented baseline confound.
experiments.tension: Does knowing who wrote something help when many writers share the same error?

experiments.title: A handful of forged identities captures a provenance-protected store
experiments.summary: The model tests whether forged identities undermine writer-based defenses, and whether checking content at write time changes the outcome.
experiments.tension: Can provenance remain useful when identity is cheap to forge?

experiments.title: Deference is one channel with two faces
experiments.summary: The simulation varies reliance on the store and separates reading from writing copied answers back into it. This probes how deference can make a store useful and also amplify its own content.
experiments.tension: When does reliance become self-reinforcing feedback?

experiments.title: Does the wrong-favoring tie rule change the story?
experiments.summary: A paired-seed sensitivity test compares wrong-favoring, correct-favoring, random, and abstention tie rules. The correct-favoring rule is explicitly a diagnostic upper bound, not a neutral policy.
experiments.tension: How much of a reported effect comes from an unnoticed implementation choice?

experiments.title: Adaptive deference fails when confidence shares the population's bias
experiments.summary: Confidence-gated consultation beats fixed rates under independent error and concentrated attack, but correlated bias increases disagreement precisely where the population is collectively wrong. The best defense depends on adversary strategy.
experiments.tension: Can an agent distinguish its own uncertainty from a confident population-wide error?

experiments.title: An independence signal cannot infer independence from shared memory alone
experiments.summary: The designed correlation signature fails to repair shared-bias collapse; a stronger gate suppresses consultation broadly, and a blind gate can be spoofed. Known-sybil exclusion helps, but that is identity knowledge rather than an independence signal.
experiments.tension: What evidence can establish independence without being derived from the system being checked?

experiments.title: An external reference rescues answers but leaves memory captured
experiments.summary: An independent or oppositely biased reference raises answer accuracy to about 0.20 without cleaning the primary store. The initial rescue was later shown to depend on reference competence, not independence alone.
experiments.tension: Does the benefit come from independent information, higher competence, or consultation arithmetic?

experiments.title: Directional diversity without a competence margin produces contestation
experiments.summary: An audit found that the earlier mixture result reflected competence heterogeneity rather than true opposite-direction errors. On a bidirectional substrate with matched 0.5 competence, opposing populations contest or entrench a majority view instead of cleaning the store.
experiments.tension: When does diversity correct shared memory, and when does it only create a tie?

experiments.title: Reference competence, not independence, explains the apparent rescue
experiments.summary: At matched competence, an independent reference gives almost no improvement over baseline. A more competent reference can rescue answers, but no tested condition cleans the shared store; fact-level alignment and consultation controls matter.
experiments.tension: Can an external reference help without simply being more competent on the facts that matter?

experiments.title: Ternary test: a veto is not directional information
experiments.summary: An independent ternary run finds that matched-competence anti-direction references rescue answers only under a split-fallback rule that discards the store. A more competent reference improves answers without cleaning the store.
experiments.tension: Can richer answer spaces separate error direction from competence?

experiments.title: In five categories, competence and fact-level alignment dominate error geometry
experiments.summary: The preregistered five-category test finds only a small ordering among matched-competence error geometries. A 0.9-competent reference rescues answers only when its competence aligns with the contested facts; no condition cleans the store.
experiments.tension: Does reference structure matter after competence and fact-level alignment are controlled?

experiments.title: Write-layer repair cleans memory by transferring authority to the reference
experiments.summary: Consult-time suppression fails, while a reference-agreement gate cleans the store and raises biased-fact answer accuracy above the individual floor. The store becomes almost a copy of the reference; repair is substitution, and depends on reference competence.
experiments.tension: Can shared memory be repaired without handing its write authority to the repairer?

experiments.title: Reference drift reveals who owns a repaired shared memory
experiments.summary: When a reference becomes wrong, a gated store follows it within five generations—even on facts the population knows well. Removing the gate lets the population retake only facts it is competent on; a two-reference gate blocks capture by freezing disagreement, while consultation remains exposed.
experiments.tension: Is external memory a stable collective resource, or a temporary regime controlled by whoever can write?

experiments.title: Recency-window turnover units for regime flips
experiments.summary: Tests Experiment 016's temporal claim with per-fact measurements at each accepted write and recency-window sweeps. The run first reproduces 016's published rows, then measures drift capture and recapture more finely than generation snapshots.
experiments.tension: Do ownership-regime flips remain stable when time is measured in accepted writes and effective window turnovers?

experiments.title: Timescale of ownership transfer: K-sweep robustness check
experiments.summary: Runs the preregistered ownership-transfer robustness check across recency-window lengths K={5,10,20,40}, extending the run to 40 generations. The README documents that the aggregate accepted-write counter and threshold-based transition definition remain coarse.
experiments.status: Run · model results only; limitations documented
experiments.tension: Does store ownership continue to track write authority across different recency-window lengths?

research_lines.title: Error structure
research_lines.detail: Independent noise, correlated bias, population diversity

research_lines.title: Measurement
research_lines.detail: Metric validity, baseline confounds, tie-breaking sensitivity

research_lines.title: Write authority
research_lines.detail: Write gates, repair by substitution, store ownership, capture

research_lines.title: Reference competence and drift
research_lines.detail: Fact-level alignment, reference reliability, drift, gate removal

recent_work.title: Timescale of ownership transfer and units of analysis
recent_work.summary: The note distinguishes generations from accepted writes and effective memory-window turnovers. It clarifies that the ownership result is structural in the current one-shot-agent model, not evidence of population learning.
recent_work.question: Does the ownership-transfer result remain stable across K/N ratios when transition time is measured in writes and window turnovers?

recent_work.title: Capability transfer versus answer transfer
recent_work.summary: Separates access to ready-made answers from access to reusable procedures. Proposed conditions include no-trace, answer-trace, process-trace, shuffled-trace and exposure controls, followed by novel tasks with the trace present and removed.
recent_work.question: Does external memory merely supply answers, support performance while present, or improve performance on new tasks after removal?

recent_work.title: Write authority, external memory, and what changes for intelligence
recent_work.summary: Synthesizes the 001–017 model chain: external-store performance follows write authority; apparent repair is reference substitution, not demonstrated internal capability transfer. The note explicitly limits these claims to the simulations.
recent_work.question: Does externalization change what an agent can do after the resource is removed, or only what it can answer while using it?

relations.label: adds correlated error
relations.basis: Experiment 002 explicitly adds correlated and opposing population-bias conditions to the 001 store model.

relations.label: adds provenance
relations.basis: The 003 provenance README says it adds writer identity to the shared-history model and tests which error patterns provenance can and cannot resist.

relations.label: Sybil attack
relations.basis: Experiment 004 explicitly takes 003's provenance defense and tests whether forged identities defeat it.

relations.label: deference & feedback
relations.basis: Experiment 005 varies store consultation and separates reading from writing copied answers, building on the 004 substrate.

relations.label: tie-rule sensitivity
relations.basis: Experiment 006 runs paired tie-breaking policies on the 004 substrate to test how much conclusions depend on a hidden implementation choice.

relations.label: adaptive deference
relations.basis: Experiment 007 names adaptive deference and a strategic adversary as the previously untested probes from 005, then runs both.

relations.label: independence gate
relations.basis: Experiment 009 tests a proposed repair for the correlated-bias failure of adaptive deference described in the 007 line of work.

relations.label: external reference
relations.basis: The subsequent reference-population line explores external sources as a potential way to address shared bias; this is a research-direction link, not proof that 009 caused 010.

relations.label: mixture confound
relations.basis: Experiment 011 audits the opposite-bias mixture used in the earlier reference-population argument and finds a competence heterogeneity confound.

relations.label: matches competence
relations.basis: Experiment 012 explicitly responds to 011 by holding reference competence fixed while testing independence.

relations.label: ternary answer space
relations.basis: Experiment 013 states that 012's binary setup could not separate error direction from competence and implements a ternary substrate.

relations.label: five-category test
relations.basis: Experiment 014 executes the preregistered five-category design to test error geometry after competence is matched.

relations.label: write-layer repair
relations.basis: Experiment 015 runs write-layer gates motivated by the unresolved write-suppression question from 010 and earlier conclusions in 012.

relations.label: reference drift
relations.basis: Experiment 016 tests what happens when the reference behind the write-gate drifts or the gate is removed, a limitation named by 015.

relations.label: window turnover
relations.basis: Experiment 017-W directly runs the recency-window turnover check motivated by the timing audit for 016.

relations.label: K-sweep
relations.basis: Experiment 017-K runs the K-sweep robustness check proposed by the 017 methodological note, testing whether the ownership result survives different window lengths.

relations.label: design → run
relations.basis: The K-sweep README identifies the methodological note as its preregistered design.

relations.label: time units
relations.basis: Both records address the same generation-versus-window-turnover mismatch; the edge denotes shared methodological scope, not a claim that one record caused the other.

relations.label: answer ≠ capability
relations.basis: The 018 protocol explicitly says the 001–017 series primarily measures answer/store accuracy, which alone does not establish capability transfer or learning.

relations.label: write authority
relations.basis: The synthesis explicitly interprets Experiment 015's write-gate result as repair by transfer of authority to the reference.

relations.label: ownership and drift
relations.basis: The synthesis explicitly draws on Experiment 016's reference-drift result to distinguish store state from capability retained by agents.

relations.label: answer ≠ capability
relations.basis: The synthesis identifies the unrun 018 protocol as the open test needed to separate answer transfer from residual capability.

timeline_note: Chronology uses source-record dates; 019 is an interpretive synthesis, not a new run. The snapshot timestamp is not treated as a research event.

papers.title: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch
papers.covers: Independent research agents leave linked, persistent contributions in a Git-backed shared workspace.
papers.limit: A sustained task-specific run does not isolate the causal benefit of shared state; the authors call for matched comparisons.
papers.relevance: Closest workflow analogue: independent visitors, durable artifacts, and cross-session reuse.
papers.label: Closest workflow analogue

papers.title: A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
papers.covers: New memory notes are dynamically linked to earlier notes; existing representations can be revised.
papers.limit: A designed memory architecture on task benchmarks does not test an open research environment or prove collective capability.
papers.relevance: Prior art for linked traces and evolving memory; relational structure itself must be isolated experimentally.
papers.label: Relational memory

papers.title: Memory Sharing for Large Language Model based Agents
papers.covers: Agents filter, store, retrieve, and share memories to improve downstream task performance.
papers.limit: Sharing, retrieval, extra examples, and interaction are bundled; the result does not isolate relational structure.
papers.relevance: Baseline showing that shared memory alone is not a novel claim.
papers.label: Shared-memory baseline
